```{r}
#| echo: false

#| message: false

library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
library(glue)
library(gganimate)
```

```{r}
# custom theme 
theme_custom <- function() {
  theme_minimal() + 
  theme(
    text = element_text(family = "Avenir"), 
    plot.title = element_text(family = "Avenir"), 
    axis.text = element_text(family="Avenir")
  )
}

theme_set(theme_custom())
```

For a more interactive view of the visitor data one can also check out [this one](https://mika-long.github.io/national_park/). 

First we load the data^[which was obtained from https://www.responsible-datasets-in-context.com/posts/np-data/?tab=explore-the-data]. The file is not quite ready to be merged with other ones, so we make changes to it.  

```{r}
df <- read.csv(file = "US-National-Parks_Use_1979-2023_By-Month.csv") %>% 
  tibble(.) %>% 
  mutate(ParkName = str_remove(ParkName, "NP.*$")) |>
  mutate(ParkName = trimws(ParkName)) %>% 
  mutate(Region = trimws(Region))

knitr::kable(head(df))
```

---
# Let's animate things! 

The following is a static graph: 

```{r}
#| column: page 

df %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = Month, y = RecreationVisits, color = Year, group = Year)) + 
  geom_line() + 
  facet_wrap(~UnitCode) + 
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:12, labels = 1:12) + 
  scale_color_viridis_c()
```
---


Let's try animating this! 

First, let's see what the static one looks like: 

```{r}
df %>% filter(ParkName == "Acadia") %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = Month, y = RecreationVisits, color = Year, group = Year)) + 
  geom_line() + 
  scale_color_viridis_c()+ 
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:12, labels = 1:12) + 
  scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) paste0(x/1000, "K"))
```

This is the animated version: 

```{r}
df %>% filter(ParkName == "Acadia") %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = Month, y = RecreationVisits, color = Year, group = Year)) + 
  geom_line(linewidth=1.5) + 
  scale_color_viridis_c()+ 
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:12, labels = 1:12) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) paste0(x/1000, "K")) + 
  labs(title = 'Year: {frame_time}') + 
  transition_time(Year) + 
  shadow_mark(past = T, future = F, alpha = 0.1)
```

We can also do it for the entire United States: 

```{r}
df %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = Month, y = RecreationVisits, color = Year, group = Year)) + 
  geom_line() + 
  facet_wrap(~UnitCode) + 
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:12, labels = 1:12) + 
  scale_color_viridis_c() + 
  scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) paste0(x/1000, "K")) + 
  labs(title = 'Year: {frame_time}') + 
  transition_time(Year) + 
  shadow_mark(past = T, future = F, alpha = 0.1)
```
